note: States follow the vocabulary in 05_ACCEPTANCE_GATES.md. Unknown is never PASS. A gate covering several models is recorded per the weakest applicable scope, and the scope field names it.

gates.name: inventory/scope
gates.scope: all 17 model ids, 29 checkpoint variants, protocol assignment per registry
gates.detail: MODEL_MATRIX.csv has 29 rows across 17 distinct model_id values, matching the registry count read directly. Each row records upstream URL/commit, checkpoint path and status, interpreter, last run id, whether that run is a model run, coverage, candidate depth, gate status, decision and blocker. Deferred (csmcir, sprc) and BLOCKED rows are present and labelled rather than dropped, so a model does not disappear because it has no run.

gates.name: input correctness
gates.scope: all active models; no per-model native-vs-adapter input differential was executed in this session
gates.reject_reason: No ID/text/pixel/token/mask differential against a pinned upstream reference was run this session. Earlier rounds audited protocol assignment and adapter wiring, which is not full input parity. Static reading and matching shapes do not constitute G1 evidence, so PASS would be unsupported.

gates.name: forward/scoring
gates.scope: all models; no forward pass was validated against a reference this session
gates.reject_reason: No new forward pass was validated. The BLAS sensitivity measurement drove each adapter's score() on synthetic float32 matrices, which is arithmetic-path evidence for G7, not evidence that any model's forward output matches its native implementation.

gates.name: policy/identity
gates.scope: the identity/policy CODE, verified by tests, PLUS eight published runs recorded at identity schema v2 (see G5); every other artifact on disk still predates v2 and is labelled 'unknown (predates identity v2)'
gates.detail:
Identity v2 records blas_threads_pinned, the verified blas_pin_capability (setter promoted only after a runtime readback), query_scope_resolution, query_order_identity and cache_verify_mode, and stamps identity_schema_version 2. Runs differing in any of those mint different group ids (6 identity tests). A recorded artifact predating v2 is labelled 'unknown (predates identity v2)' with group_id null and is never silently regrouped. IMPORTANT LIMIT: no published artifact carries v2 yet, so this is a PASS about the code path, not about any existing artifact. Only the encoder run in RUN_LOG.csv (identity_schema_version 2) exercises it end to end.

UPDATED 2026-11-09T08:05:00+07:00: the earlier scope sentence said 'NO published run yet carries identity v2'. That is no longer true - the eight rerun models now each record identity_schema_version 2 with confidence 'full' (G5 evidence). The state stays PASS and the reject_reason is unchanged; only the stale scope claim was corrected, because a document that asserts no artifact carries v2 while eight do is the kind of false statement that gets discovered later.

gates.name: cache/resume/fallback
gates.scope: the cache-integrity and backfill mechanisms, by negative test
gates.detail: Negative tests prove rejection of: same-shape changed content, truncated file, stale sidecar shape, recorded byte_length mismatch, and a backfilled target rank that disagrees with the recorded run (BackfillRankDisagreement, reported as TOPK_EXPORT_BLOCKED). A legacy cache with no digest still loads but is reported content_digest 'absent' / verified false and is never called validated. NOTE: because the feature-cache key is the identity digest, every pre-v2 feature cache is now unreachable by design, so --resume cannot bridge the schema change; that is correct but it means no historical run can be backfilled.

gates.name: clean run/coverage
gates.scope: the eight rerun models (encoder, conesep, habit, intent, hint, limn, ptha_mtst, tme) under the recorded BLAS policy; the other 21 registry variants remain BLOCKED or DEFERRED with reasons in MODEL_MATRIX.csv and are NOT covered by this PASS
gates.detail: Eight full runs completed under the recorded policy, one GPU job at a time, each verified from its artifact by verify_run.py rather than from console output. Seven scored 6003/6003; limn scored 6001/6003 (coverage 0.9996668332500417) with two queries explicitly unscored and reasoned (7:3038, 7:3790 - 'category unresolved has no adapter embedding scope'), never rounded to 100%. Every run records blas_threads_pinned=1 with blas_pin_capability verifiable and cache_verify_mode=full, and identifies as identity schema v2 with confidence full. Invariants per run: every in-scope query has a rank or an explicit reason; candidate rows strictly ordered by score; candidate target_rank equals the metric path's for all rows. Caveat that keeps this scoped rather than cohort-wide: ptha_mtst's ENCODE path cannot be pinned at all (its interpreter is MKL-only and mkl_set_num_threads segfaults it), so that run is not equivalent to an OpenBLAS-pinned one; and no wall time here is a baseline (two other lanes were active throughout - G8 stays NOT_RUN).

gates.name: rank/export
gates.scope: the eight rerun models, all at Top-100 depth on every supported condition and query; models with no composition adapter or no staged checkpoint are outside this gate
gates.detail: All eight rerun models export Top-100. Manifests record depth=100, record_count 6003 against expected 6003 and partial=false for encoder, conesep, habit, intent, hint, ptha_mtst and tme; limn records record_count 6001 against expected 6003 with partial=true, which is the honest shape for its two unscored queries. verify_run.py checked, for 18009 candidate rows across encoder/conesep/habit/intent/hint/tme and the corresponding rows for limn and ptha_mtst: positions are valid gallery indices, every row is strictly ordered by score under the recorded tie policy, and target_rank equals the metric path's rank - 0 order violations, 0 target-rank mismatches. The previous cohort state (four models at depth 50, four with no export) is superseded by these eight runs; those older artifacts are retained, not deleted.

gates.name: optimization parity
gates.scope: BLAS thread-count parity per adapter, and query-axis parallelism; no speedup is claimed
gates.detail: Measured, seed 20261109, gallery 3000, 8 queries, 6 planted near-ties per query, BLAS 1 vs 20 through the runtime setter: encoder changed 29/400 top-50 ranks (max |drank| 5, 6/8 tie clusters reordered, max |dscore| 1.788e-07); conesep, ptha_mtst, habit, intent, hint, limn and tme were bit-identical (0/400, 0.000e+00). Mechanism isolated: a batched GEMM (M>1) is thread-variant, a single-query matvec is not; np.linalg.norm(axis=1) is invariant. NO SPEEDUP IS CLAIMED because no uncontaminated timing was taken (see G8).

gates.name: measured performance
gates.reject_reason: Two other lanes were running during this session. The one available measurement (encoder, RUN_LOG.csv) states in its own wall_time_note that it was 'measured under concurrent load from two other lanes - not a baseline', and records throughput as not_measured. A contaminated baseline is worse than none, so no performance claim is made.

gates.detail: Re-run live against 127.0.0.1:5173, all exit 0: cold 3 checks (registry card 17 entries matching /api/models, 17 rendered rows, 14 blocker disclosures reading '<n> lý do'), composition 8 checks (9 rows fit their box, expansion does not widen the table, benchmark view never dead-ends, and the banner cannot claim Top-K unavailable over rows that have it while its count must equal the rows rendered), mobile 4 checks plus 1 documented SKIP, samples 2 checks (badge-vs-ranks agreement). 13 node contract tests pass. /api/models serves 17 entries and all 17 render.

Harness at 1440x900, 1920x1080 and 390x844 reports body.scrollWidth == innerWidth (no page-level horizontal overflow) and 0 cells narrower than 60px holding 200+ characters. Not verified: physical DPI/scaling of a 27-inch monitor, and an independent accessibility audit.

gates.name: integration/release
gates.scope: tests, build, served asset, remote SHA
gates.reject_reason: The guard is RED: test_no_release_document_points_at_a_superseded_source_sha fails because TESTED_SOURCE_SHA is 80842661 while production has changed (1 failed, 7 passed). Advancing it requires a full serial sweep, which cannot run while a GPU evaluation is in flight. The other halves of this gate do hold: tests pass (25 evaluator + 5 clip4cir + all capability suites + 10 topk + 27 throughput + 3 cache), npm run build exits 0, and the served asset index-9MwV5MAk.js matches dist/assets exactly. Until the sweep lands, the revision is not gateable.

gates.name: coordination
gates.scope: lane ownership, deduplicated work, single GPU owner
gates.detail: One recorded deviation, stated rather than hidden: four lanes ran concurrently at one point against a stated cap of three. The fourth was stood down and its task completed under the cap. File ownership held: the five integration commits are lane-pure (evaluator / CLIP4Cir / evidence / frontend / airknow), and the one file two lanes touched -- registry/models.yaml -- was split at hunk level so no commit contains another lane's change. GPU: a single composition_eval owned the device throughout; no duplicate evaluator was launched.

summary.headline: 9 PASS, 1 FAIL, 3 NOT_RUN. G5 and G6 moved because eight full runs now exist under the recorded policy with Top-100 export, each verified from its artifact. G1/G2 keep NOT_RUN: no native-vs-adapter input or forward differential was executed. G8 keeps NOT_RUN: every wall time was taken with two other lanes active and is not a baseline. G11 keeps FAIL: TESTED_SOURCE_SHA still cannot advance without a serial sweep. G5's PASS is scoped to the eight rerun models, and it is not cohort-wide.
